title: EPOC
description: This dataset comprises 128-channel EEG recordings from 98 participants recruited from the COVIDOM/NAPKON-POP cohort, all with a history of confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study investigates neurophysiological correlates of Post-COVID-19 condition, focusing on self-reported cognitive symptoms, fatigue, anxiety, depression, and sleep quality. Participants underwent EEG recording during resting-state and cognitive tasks including a Psychomotor Vigilance Task, alongside standardized questionnaires (FACIT-Fatigue, HADS, PSQI) and neuropsychological testing.
methods_description: EEG was recorded using a 128-channel equidistant electrode cap (Easycap GmbH) with an actiCHamp Plus amplifier (Brain Products GmbH) at a sampling rate of 1000 Hz and amplitude resolution of 0.1 μV. Electrode impedances were maintained below 20 kΩ, with a nose reference and two diagonally placed EOG electrodes beneath each eye. Participants completed the Trail Making Test, EEG recording during cognitive tasks and resting-state, and post-session questionnaires assessing fatigue, depression, anxiety, and sleep quality.
